items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: The Nifty index fell for a third straight day, closing lower amid rising market volatility. Analysts suggest markets may face continued pressure due to oil prices and bond yields. Foreign portfolio investors and domestic institutional investors were net buyers of shares on Wednesday. The Indian rupee ended little changed, supported by the Reserve Bank of India. SAIL and LIC Housing Finance are currently in the F&O ban period.

items.title: Stocks in news: Swiggy, Adani Ports, IDFC First Bank, Hexaware Technologies and Sun Pharma
items.description: Indian markets experienced a sharp decline on Wednesday due to global factors.  Technical analysis suggests further downside potential for the Nifty index.  Several companies like Swiggy and Adani Ports are in focus today.  Hyundai Motor India aims to regain its market position with new launches.  ONGC is reviewing its Venezuelan assets after receiving US approval.

items.title: Zerodha unit gets nod for merchant banking
items.description: On September 1, Zerodha Corporate Advisors secured approval from Sebi to function as a merchant banker, following their application back in April. This pivotal approval enables the firm to facilitate initial public offerings and handle various capital market activities. Although the complete registration process with the regulator remains in progress, Zerodha Corporate Advisors is gearing up to launch its new merchant banking services shortly.

items.title: Small finance banks' asset quality to improve, GNPA to drop by 120 basis points by March 2027: Crisil
items.description: Small finance banks anticipate improved asset quality this financial year.  Gross non-performing assets are projected to decline significantly by March 2027.  This improvement stems from microfinance portfolio recovery and stable non-microfinance growth.  Tighter underwriting practices have strengthened borrower selection in microfinance portfolios.  Borrower over-indebtedness caused past credit stress in microfinance books.

items.title: Insurers plan floor for fire cover to avoid large burns
items.description: Non-life insurers are considering a minimum rate for fire insurance's natural catastrophe component. This move follows concerns about steep discounts exposing the industry and reinsurers to losses. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India chairman also expressed worries about insurer financial health. Aggressive pricing and recent fire losses in Gujarat have fueled these discussions. Insurers aim to restrict discounts to the flexible fire rate component.

items.title: 'Revolver' misfire hits credit card issuers: India's credit card boom sees lower bank profits
items.description: Credit card profits are shrinking for Indian banks as spending rises. Customers now use cards more for payments than borrowing, reducing interest income. Interest-bearing balances have significantly fallen as a percentage of total card spending. This trend is impacting major lenders like HDFC Bank and SBI Cards. Analysts predict further profit margin declines in the coming years.

items.title: FIIs are showering India with billions. Why are Nifty stocks missing the party?
items.description: Despite foreign investors infusing billions into Indian equities, benchmark indices struggle to keep pace. Inflows in the primary market are notable but fail to directly uplift listed stocks. Selective purchases are occurring in large mid-cap stocks while financials and IT remain ignored. Domestic investors are a crucial pillar for market resilience, necessitating consistent secondary market activity for a comprehensive rally.

items.title: Sensex rises over 300 points, Nifty near 24,000 as US bonds yields slightly ease. Why is caution still warranted?
items.description: Indian stock markets traded higher on Thursday, with key indices showing gains. The Sensex rose over 300 points, reaching 76,900 on its weekly expiry day. Nifty 50 also gained over 83 points, beginning the session near 23,998. Broader markets followed suit, with midcap and smallcap indices experiencing upward movement. This positive start occurred after a significant decline in the previous trading session.

items.title: Power Grid shares gain 1.5% after firm wins Rs 3,244 crore inter-state transmission system project. Should you buy?
items.description: Shares of Power Grid experienced an uptick after the company secured an important transmission project aimed at facilitating power evacuation from Rajasthan. This endeavor will incorporate the establishment of HVDC terminals and a long-distance transmission line. Power Grid's successful bid for this vital project reflects its strategic growth, amidst varying stock performance observed in recent months.

items.title: Persistent Systems shares fall over 3% as board gives nod for $1.25 billion fundraise. Check details
items.description: Persistent Systems approved plans to raise up to $1.25 billion through debt and up to $450 million via equity-linked instruments, subject to approvals. The IT firm reported strong bookings and revenue growth in Q1, though profit declined due to forex losses. Shares have gained 21% over six months.

items.title: Swiggy shares fall 2%, down for 3rd session, as MSCI set to remove stock from Global Standard Indexes from September 7
items.description: Shares of Swiggy experienced a decline following MSCI's decision to exclude the company from global indexes, prompted by its shift to full Indian ownership and control. The new foreign ownership constraints limit further investments. Swiggy is targeting robust adjusted EBITDA growth by FY31, even as it reported a net loss while revenues showed an uptick in Q1 FY27.

items.title: Kwick Forensic Solutions shares debut at 67% premium over IPO price on BSE SME platform
items.description: The IPO, which opened for subscription on August 27 and closed on August 31, witnessed an extraordinary response from investors, with the issue subscribed a staggering 289 times overall.

items.title: Lumino Industries shares list at 34% premium over IPO price
items.description: The Rs 700-crore IPO was offered in a price band of Rs 78–Rs 82 per share. The issue comprised a fresh issue of Rs 500 crore, involving 6.10 crore shares, and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs 200 crore, involving 2.44 crore shares sold by promoters Devendra Goel and Jay Goel.

items.title: Hitachi Energy emerges as potential ‘buy’ on strong order inflows, earnings visibility
items.description: Hitachi Energy shares have surged significantly this year on robust revenue growth.  The company secured new orders for battery storage and data centers.  Its substantial order book provides a strong near-term earnings driver.  Future growth is anticipated from high-voltage direct current projects and capacity expansion.  Analysts have revised price targets upwards, reflecting strong future prospects.

items.title: Happiest Minds shares fall for 5th day as merger concerns weigh
items.description: The stock of Happiest Minds Technologies has experienced a significant downturn due to uncertainty related to the ITC Infotech integration. Promoters will cash in, whereas minority shareholders are set to receive shares in the merger. The merger is expected to enhance long-term profitability. Yet, HDFC Securities has downgraded the stock, pointing out the lack of a takeover premium and the anticipated integration time.

items.title: MSCI to drop Swiggy from global indices on September 7
items.description: Global index providers MSCI and FTSE are set to revise Swiggy's index treatment shortly. MSCI is removing Swiggy from global indices, which will lead to considerable passive outflows. Additionally, FTSE has modified Swiggy's investability weight due to foreign ownership limits. Together, these alterations are projected to trigger passive outflows surpassing $350 million, causing Swiggy shares to drop on Wednesday after the news broke.
